title: OP Harmonizer (declarative)
description: A harmonizer DEFINITION: declarative JSON that selects fields out of a source document. A local file under api.harmonizers.dir is the same shape as a harmonizer fetched over HTTP, so this schema covers both. A harmonizer names the HANDLER it runs under via `mode`; it carries no code. Validation here is deliberately dialect-agnostic: each extraction rule must be a selector string or an array of rule objects, but the KEYS inside a rule object (selector/attribute, column, ...) belong to the individual handler and are not constrained here.

//.description: Authoring comment. Ignored by the loader.

id.description: Stable identifier for this harmonizer (conventionally a URL or 'harmonizer/<name>'). Site harmonizers are KEYED by file basename at discovery; the id is identity, not the lookup key.

type.description: Artifact kind. Always 'harmonizer' — a definition claiming another type is a category error. Discovery stamps the value when absent.

mode.description: The HANDLER this harmonizer runs under (e.g. 'html', 'csv'). Not resolved at load time: discovery order between handlers.dir and harmonizers.dir is not guaranteed, and an unknown mode falls through to the registry's default-handler dispatch.

schema.description: The extraction map. `subject` is required — it is the section every handler reads; additional top-level sections (e.g. 'hashtag') are typed statement groups the handler may consume.

section.description: One extraction section: field name -> rule. A rule is a string (e.g. 's': 'source'), a rule object in the handler's dialect, or an array mixing the two (the json handler's 's': ['url', '@id'] and 'image': [{...}, 'image.url'] are both legal). Which keys a rule object carries belongs to the individual handler.
